alternative_architecture.description: No replacement architecture is warranted. The layered separation of durable definition, immutable evidence, derived conformance, and fail-closed authorization is sound and worth keeping. The fix is sequencing and proportion, not redesign: pause expanding the planning/provider-abstraction surface, add the minimum write-capable execution slice, and close the GDD-drift-for-unexecuted-tasks gap, before resuming Milestone 2-style investment.
alternative_architecture.why_better: n/a — reorganizing priority order solves the identified problems without discarding demonstrably good state-authority design work.

structured_output.architecture_summary: The pipeline separates four state layers cleanly: (1) durable definition (`Tasks/*.yaml`, schema 2.0, no mutable status), (2) immutable point-in-time evidence (delivery/baseline/revalidation records under `Pipeline/TaskGraph/evidence/`, git-blob/hash-bound), (3) deterministically derived current conformance (`current_conformance.py`, computed from committed HEAD, never stored as authority), and (4) explicit fail-closed dispatch authorization (`taskcontrol authorize` currently denies everything). Reconciliation is a separate immutable-snapshot layer that is documented to propose, not apply, graph deltas. A new provider-neutral `AgentRuntime` (generic `AgentInvocationRequest`/`AgentResult`) sits below a thin `TaskExecution` layer that is supposed to carry NSC task identity without contaminating the generic runtime. Today AgentRuntime only supports empty-capability, repository-read, and repository-search invocations for Claude and Codex, used solely to run this very ArchitectureReview process; repository write, approved command execution, Git branch/worktree creation, GER wiring, and Unity execution by an agent are all unimplemented. No Milestone 3 (supervisor/Git/GitHub), Milestone 4 (production GER+Unity validation), or Milestone 5 (continuous autonomy) exists in code.
structured_output.biggest_uncertainty: Whether the team intends the next real slice to include write capability soon (making my core critique moot within days) or whether Milestone 2 planning/decomposition work is about to be built first as CURRENT_STATE.md's routing table currently suggests — I could not find any code or ADR yet describing a concrete write-capability design, so I cannot tell if this is already underway off-repository or genuinely not yet planned.
do_not_build_yet: Milestone 2 RAG/Scanner/Progressive Decomposer/Artifact Authority Gate as currently sequenced next — it adds planning sophistication on top of an execution path that still cannot write a line of code.
Further OpenAI/Codex production parity or a Claude-vs-Codex comparison pipeline beyond what already exists for ArchitectureReview.
Additional provider-trust-boundary hardening beyond what is already implemented.
Any dependency-derived `taskcontrol ready` or dispatch-authorization policy until at least one real ticket has gone through write-capable execution.
Parallel workers, claims/leases, or worktree orchestration.
Automatic/global GDD impact analysis (fine to defer, but the narrower per-task drift-flagging gap noted above should not be deferred as long).

evidence.observation: Repository write, approved command execution, and non-null token limits remain rejected before launch; only empty/read/search capabilities exist for both providers, used solely for ArchitectureReview.
TaskExecutionRunner.run only writes an audit JSON file and forwards the same invocation to AgentRunner — no Git, evidence, or dispatch wiring exists yet.

GDD canon-hash comparison (current_canon_hash) is only evaluated inside the per-record loop for tasks that already have committed evidence records; tasks with zero records return not_delivered without any canon-drift check.
acceptance_criteria and gdd_evidence embed literal quoted GDD text/section references with no hash or version field binding them to the current GDD.

Documents Stage 4C/4D (dual provider adapters, ArchitectureReview migration) as the most recent work as of 2026-08-23, with explicit statements that no real gameplay task execution, Unity validation by a model, or dispatch authorization exists yet.

States Milestone 1 completed 2026-08-21 and current work is dated 2026-08-23, i.e. roughly three days produced the entire Stage 3/4 AgentRuntime/provider/ArchitectureReview infrastructure with no gameplay ticket delivered in that window.
Grep for diff/delta/apply logic found no dedicated reconciliation-delta-to-graph apply tool; only the one-time bootstrap seeder exists.

gdd_iteration_concerns: Only tasks with a committed evidence record get GDD-hash-based staleness detection (`needs_revalidation`); the 36 not-yet-implemented task contracts have zero live binding to the GDD text they quote, so an edit to `Docs/GDD/No_Safe_Circle_GDD.md` today would not surface which planned tasks are now describing outdated design.

The project explicitly discourages running full reconciliation after every GDD edit ('routine GDD iteration should eventually use reviewed, scoped impact analysis') but has not built that scoped alternative, leaving a real gap between 'don't do the expensive thing routinely' and 'have a cheap thing to do instead.'

Task contracts embed literal GDD quotes inline (`gdd_evidence`, `acceptance_criteria[].reference/requirement`) as copied text rather than as a live retrieval pointer, so even a correct-at-authoring-time contract can silently diverge from the canon it claims to represent with no mechanical way to notice short of manual re-reading.
human_intervention_points: Required human Play Mode approval on evidence records before a task can derive as `conformant`.
`taskcontrol authorize` is deny-by-default; enabling any dispatch policy requires a future human-approved decision.
PR/branch merge to `main` is manual by design; no automerge exists or is planned soon.

NSC-003 (the suggested first gameplay anchor) is explicitly flagged as requiring human resolution of multiple design ambiguities (input-action ownership, arbitration among systems, click-vs-hold semantics) before any worker should receive it.
Any Artifact Authority Gate decision (AUTHORIZED/REJECTED/NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW) once that layer is built.
Any second reconciliation event, since the delta-to-graph apply boundary is documented as requiring explicit review.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Provider-trust-boundary hardening against malicious/polymorphic subclasses, cycle bombs, and 64-container nesting limits defends against adversarial input in a system whose only current input source is the single trusted developer's own local invocations (ADR-038 itself calls this a 'trusted single-user boundary').

Building a full parallel OpenAI/Codex provider adapter with equivalent capability mapping before the Claude path has executed a single real gameplay task doubles maintenance surface for a comparison ('Claude-versus-Codex') that has no pipeline to consume it yet.
Ambiguous-evidence tie-breaking across multiple maximal, git-incomparable records is fully implemented and tested even though no task has ever produced conflicting evidence records in practice.

Budget ceiling constants (1,000 turns, 86,400 seconds, 10,000,000 tokens) and exhaustive JSON-schema-keyword rejection are calibrated for a hostile multi-tenant SaaS, not a single developer's bounded local coding sessions.
missing_components: Repository write / code-change capability in AgentRuntime — the actual mechanism needed for an agent to implement a gameplay feature does not exist.
Git branch/worktree creation, claiming, and Draft PR automation (Milestone 3) — entirely undesigned in code beyond a markdown sketch.

Any wiring between AgentRuntime/TaskExecution and the existing, already-proven Assignment 6 GER repair loop or the existing Unity clean-test runner (`Pipeline/Testing/run_unity_tests_clean.ps1`) — these exist in isolation and are not connected.
A GDD-drift/impact-analysis mechanism for not-yet-implemented task contracts (currently only evidenced tasks get canon-hash checking).
A real, tested reconciliation delta diff/review/apply tool for post-bootstrap graph changes (only the one-time seeder exists).

deliverables: Add a narrowly scoped repository_write capability to AgentRuntime, gated to a single task's declared exclusive_resources/paths and a dedicated branch/worktree.
Wire that capability to one already-unambiguous ready task (not NSC-003, which needs human design resolution first) — e.g. NSC-037 or NSC-024 — rather than inventing a new task.
Reuse the existing Assignment 6 GER repair loop and the existing `Pipeline/Testing/run_unity_tests_clean.ps1` runner instead of re-architecting a new evaluator.
Produce a real committed delivery evidence record (not a baseline) for that task through the new pipeline, with human Play Mode approval as already required.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md/DECISIONS.md with what actually broke or was missing when trying this for real.
next_slice.proof_of_value: A single real gameplay task delivered branch-to-merge by the new AgentRuntime/TaskExecution machinery, with a genuine (non-baseline) delivery evidence record, is the first concrete data point on whether this pipeline shortens real development time versus doing the ticket by hand.
next_slice.title: Prove one real write-capable ticket end-to-end on a small, unambiguous task
next_slice.why: Nothing about the current architecture's leverage claim is falsifiable until an agent can actually write code through the new pipeline, get validated, and get merged. Every layer needed for that (write capability, branch creation, GER/Unity wiring) is currently missing, while the next scheduled milestone (RAG/Progressive Decomposer/Artifact Authority) adds more planning machinery on top of an execution path that doesn't exist yet.

observed_failure_solutions: Evidence-derived conformance / removal of mutable task status directly answers the prior architecture review's 8/8 'partially_unsound' finding that mutable task metadata was being treated as completion truth.
GER with runtime evidence as first-class validation input directly answers the Assignment 6 camera failure (static evaluation passed while runtime behavior was wrong).
No-op refinement counting against repair budget directly answers an observed Assignment 6 Refiner that claimed success while making no code changes.
Committed-HEAD-only authority (dirty worktree = warning, not truth) was demonstrated against a real case during Phase 3A development where uncommitted evidence was correctly ignored until committed.
overengineering: The AgentRuntime README reads like a security-audit document (rejecting polymorphic container/text subclasses, surrogate/NUL/ADS path characters, Windows reserved device names, cycle detection) for a runtime whose only live callers are the developer's own review scripts.

Provider-scoped output namespacing (`outputs/claude/`, `outputs/codex/`, atomic global `LATEST.json` pointer) with resumability per provider was built for a comparison workflow that does not exist yet.

Git-blob-SHA-level verification of every evidence artifact and conformance surface, plus acyclic basis-graph validation for revalidation chains, is thorough but was built before any task has gone through more than one revalidation cycle in practice.

Roughly 40 ADRs and multiple stage/ADR documents were produced in three days primarily describing provider-adapter plumbing and its own review tooling, which is a large documentation-to-delivered-gameplay-feature ratio.
state_and_authority_concerns: Open task contracts are not bound to any GDD version/hash, so canon drift is invisible for 36 of 37 tasks until a full reconciliation happens to re-examine them.

TaskExecutionRequest/TaskExecutionRunner exists as a schema and thin pass-through with no actual link yet to evidence records, exclusive-resource claims, or dispatch authorization — it currently just writes an audit JSON and forwards to AgentRunner, so the 'task identity above the runtime' boundary is declared but not yet load-bearing.

The reconciliation-to-graph-delta boundary (diff/review/apply) is asserted in docs/ADRs as the required authority path for any future graph change but has no implemented tool; if a second reconciliation happens today there is no deterministic apply mechanism to safely mutate `Tasks/*.yaml`.
No claim/lease mechanism exists yet, but this is appropriately scoped since only one worker is contemplated right now — not currently a risk.
strong_decisions: Removing mutable `status`/`complete`/`ready` from task contracts and deriving conformance only from committed Git evidence at HEAD closes the exact failure the project's own prior architecture review found (mutable metadata treated as completion truth).

Binding evidence records to task-contract revision hash, GDD canonical-text hash, and Git blob SHAs of both the implementation surface and evidence artifacts means tampering or silent drift is detectable rather than trusted by assertion.
Treating a dirty working tree as informational only (authority is committed HEAD) prevents uncommitted/aspirational state from ever counting as delivery.
Keeping GER's runtime-evidence lesson (static PASS is not sufficient for interactive Unity behavior) as an explicit invariant, learned from a real observed failure (Assignment 6 camera).

Fail-closed `taskcontrol authorize` (deny by default) and no automatic merge/dispatch keeps a human as the actual authority until the single-ticket loop is proven, which is the right order of operations even if it is currently unexercised.

Separating generic `AgentInvocationRequest` (no task identity) from `TaskExecutionRequest` (task identity) is the correct boundary to keep ArchitectureReview/Reconciliation from being contaminated by NSC-specific concerns, and vice versa.
structural_flaws: Open (not-yet-implemented) task contracts have no GDD hash/version binding. `current_conformance.py` only checks canon drift for tasks that already have an evidence record; the other 36 contracts' embedded `gdd_evidence`/`acceptance_criteria.reference` quotes can silently go stale relative to the live GDD with no detection, contradicting the project's own stated concern that the GDD is an iterative, moving target.

The documented reconciliation 'diff/review/apply boundary' for turning a later reconciliation snapshot into approved graph changes does not exist in code — only the one-time bootstrap seeder does. The architecture depends on a mechanism that is currently a paragraph in DECISIONS.md, not a tested tool.

AgentRuntime has no repository-write or command-execution capability at all. Every downstream claim about 'autonomous development' currently terminates at read/search; the actual write path this project needs to prove leverage does not exist, and nothing in the current Stage 4 work plan schedules it next (Milestone 2 RAG/decomposition is scheduled next instead).
structured_output.throughput_assessment: Currently zero proven throughput: no gameplay ticket has been executed end-to-end through the new AgentRuntime/TaskExecution machinery. The one 'complete' task (NSC-023, camera) and the small existing DoorPrototype scripts (movement/health/mana/door) were produced through the older Assignment3/Assignment6 coursework loop and human chat sessions, then retroactively baselined into the new evidence system — they are not evidence that the new pipeline itself accelerates delivery. Meanwhile roughly three days of intensive AI-agent-driven engineering effort produced substantial provider/runtime/evidence infrastructure with no gameplay output, which is the opposite of the 'days not weeks' goal being tested against the actual product.
structured_output.verdict_reason: The state/authority discipline that exists (immutable evidence separate from mutable definition, fail-closed dispatch, committed-HEAD-only authority, no cascading LLM graph rewrites) is genuinely sound and well-tested. But two things make the current whole partially unsound rather than merely "sound but small": (1) there is a real, currently-unmitigated correctness gap — GDD-drift detection only exists for the one task (NSC-023) that already has an evidence record; the other 36 task contracts embed literal GDD quotes and references with no hash/version binding, so nothing detects or flags when a GDD edit invalidates their acceptance criteria until someone manually runs a full reconciliation, which the project explicitly discourages doing routinely; and (2) the actual leverage mechanism this project exists to prove — an agent writing code, validated, merged — has zero implementation. `AgentRuntime` still fail-closes on every repository write and command-execution request, so no gameplay code can be produced through the new pipeline today. Three days of intense engineering (per the documented 2026-08-21 → 2026-08-23 timeline) produced ~40 ADRs and 70+ Python modules of provider abstraction, adversarial trust-boundary hardening, and a second (Codex) provider adapter — all in service of a review tool that reviews the pipeline itself — while the write-capable execution path that would let this system develop No Safe Circle faster was not started. The philosophy is right; the sequencing and proportion are wrong, and the GDD-staleness gap is a genuine architectural hole, not just an unbuilt nice-to-have.
